exposure: Standardized induction protocol vs. observational management
observational group (management at the discretion of the provider)
outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission for >48 hours
cohort: 855 women ≥18 years, ≥37 weeks gestation, with intact membranes and an unfavorable cervix (Bishop score ≤6 and cervical dilation ≤2 cm) with no prior cesarean
finding: Use of a standardized induction protocol was associated with a significant reduction in neonatal morbidity and NICU admission >48 hours, without increasing the risk of cesarean delivery or maternal morbidity.
